graphEvents.label: shouldRelaunch declines with one of six named reasons
A transcript missing for one second un-arms the killer
A declined relaunch is silent because the wrapper preserves the runtime exit code

label: shouldRelaunch declines with one of six named reasons: no-file, not-armed, withdrawn, stale, hop-cap and incomplete-record.
A record armed in the future is read as stale, not fresh, because a clock that stepped back makes its age unknown.
The hop count is read as stored and never coerced, so a malformed record cannot slip under the cap.
The wrapper calls should-relaunch only after the runtime exits, and a non-zero status takes the decline path which preserves the runtime's own exit code, so a declined hop is silent.
The killer's transcript grace is 1000 ms: a transcript missing for one second makes waitForIdle return false, un-arming the session so no signal is sent.
The killer's default timeout is 30000 ms, after which a session that never goes idle is left running and the hop does not happen.
isLoopAncestor throws on a failed process-table read and the killer refuses to signal rather than guess at ancestry.
The Pi live run shows prepare, killer signal and a ready relaunch within 0.2 seconds, so the Pi failure was downstream of the relaunch.
